en: Translated by the Dharma Master Yijing, who was commissioned by imperial decree,
according to the *Tripiṭaka* on the Dharma of the Yakṣa retinue of Samjñeya (herein translated as "Correctly Knowing"). This King Samjñeya has twenty-eight yakṣas [under his command].

The Great General Buddha addressed Ānanda, saying: "These twenty-eight yakṣa generals manifest great sovereign supernatural powers and majestic virtue, capable of protecting all sentient beings throughout the worlds of the ten directions to eliminate their decline, afflictions, and calamities.
There are four yakṣa generals who dwell in the eastern direction, protecting all beings belonging to the east."
To cause those born [to this state] to be free from sorrow and suffering, their names are:
Dīrgha (the Tall), Sunetra (Beautiful Eyes), Pūrṇa (Full), and Pītaka (Yellow). Having uttered these, one should state the matter for which one seeks [their aid].
(The following cases are to be understood accordingly.)
Ānanda, there are four yakṣa generals who dwell on the southern side, protecting all sentient beings of the south and causing them to be free from sorrow and suffering.
Their names are: Saṃha (Lion), Upasaṃha (Little Lion), Śaṅkila (Conch), and Candana (Sandalwood).

Furthermore, Ānanda, there are four yakṣa generals who dwell in the western direction, protecting all sentient beings of the west and causing them to be free from sorrow and suffering; their names are as follows:
Hakli (Lion), Haklīkṣa (Lion’s Hair), Prabhūta (Mighty), and Pingala (Blue).

Furthermore, Ānanda, there are four yakṣa generals who dwell in the northern direction, protecting all sentient beings of the north and causing them to be free from sorrow and suffering. Their names are as follows:
Vīraṇa (The Able Bearer), Vīrananda (The Bearer of Joy), Udyogapāla (Valiant and Diligent Protector), and Vaiśravaṇa (The Name of the Deva).

Furthermore, Ānanda, there are four yakṣa generals, each dwelling in one of the four intermediate directions, who protect all sentient beings in those quarters, causing them to be free from sorrow and suffering. Their names are as follows:
Pañcika (who has five), Pañcāla-khaṇḍa (five locations), Sātāgirī (the level mountain), and Himavanta (the Snowy Mountains).

Furthermore, Ānanda, there are four yakṣa generals who dwell upon the earth, protecting all beings living on the ground and causing them to be free from sorrow and suffering; their names are as follows:
Bhūma (Earth), Subhūma (Excellent Earth), Kāla (Black), and Upakāla (Little Black).
Furthermore, Ānanda, there are four yakṣa generals who dwell in the air, protecting all beings who inhabit the sky and causing them to be free from sorrow and suffering; their names are as follows:
Sūrya (the Sun God), Soma (the Moon God), Agni (the Fire God), and Vāyu (the Wind God). The Buddha said: "These are the dharmas for protection;
by chanting their names as spoken, they shall guard the eight directions, above, and below, bringing benefit, peace, and security to all sentient beings.
The manifestations of these yakṣas who benefit living beings are immeasurable and boundless; this is but a brief summary. Thus spoke the Buddha.
When invoking this dharma, if one appends the phrase "come swiftly" at the end of the name, it will certainly manifest its presence without transgressing its original vow;
thus, one should seek it through repeated invocation.
This is the *Vidyārāja Yakṣa Family Dharma*.
The *Peacock Vidyārājñī Sūtra* states: "The yakṣa Suśruta dwells in the country of Nakula. (End of quotation. The Master said:
"Suśruta" means "Perfectly Cognizant" (*samyag-jñāna*) in Chinese; it is also called "Subtly Cognizant" (*praṇīta-jñāna*), and so forth.
